q: בת 70 אובחנה לאחרונה עם כולנגיוקרצינומה, אושפזה לאיזון תסמינים משניים למחלתה המתקדמת ולטיפול הכימי. תלונתה העיקרית היא בחילה אשר לא הגיבה ל- Ondansetron (Zofran) ול- Metoclopramide (Pramin). באנמנזה, מעבירה גזים, שוללת עצירות או שלשולים. כאב מאוזן תחת Targin. מה מהטיפולים הבאים מתאים?
o: Haloperidol
Escitalopram
Amantadine
Lactulose
explanation:
**Persistent nausea in advanced cancer** requires assessment of its causes and symptom treatment. Haloperidol is listed among antiemetic drugs in the oncology chapter (p. 1391).

**A. Haloperidol.** Correct, it is listed among treatments for cancer-associated nausea and therefore addresses the persistent complaint (p. 1391).
**B. Escitalopram.** Wrong, an antidepressant; the scenario does not describe a depressive syndrome whose treatment explains a solution to refractory nausea (p. 929).
**C. Amantadine.** Wrong, used in Parkinson disease, whereas the scenario concerns cancer-associated nausea rather than parkinsonian symptoms (pp. 924, 1391).
**D. Lactulose.** Wrong, an osmotic laxative targeting constipation, which the patient denies; it is not the antiemetic treatment sought (p. 1373).

The patient with advanced cholangiocarcinoma has persistent nausea after the treatments described. There is no clear evidence of constipation. Haloperidol appears as an antiemetic option, but the facts do not establish a single central mechanism (pp. 1263, 1391; clinical facts from the official stem).

Its antiemetic role makes it the option directed at the continuing complaint. Dose and monitoring must be individualized; the cited pages do not supply a dose or a guarantee of safety for this case (pp. 1263, 1391).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 924, 929, 1263, 1373, 1391.
ref: Hazzard 8e · p. 1263,1391

q: בן 88, סובל מדמנציה מתקדמת והוגדר כחולה נוטה למות על רקע מחלה זו. לאחרונה הוא אוכל מעט והצוות במחלקה הסיעודית שבה מטופל העלה אפשרות של "הזנת צינור". הוא לא השאיר הנחיות מקדימות או ייפוי כוח רפואי. מה האפשרויות החוקיות במצב זה (לפי המלצות ועד המותב)?
o: הארכת חיים מלאכותית בחולה נוטה למות הינה מנוגדת עקרונית לחוק ולכן לא מומלץ להאכיל בזונדה או PEG
הדרך המועדפת להאכלה של חולים עם דמנציה סופנית הינה ב- PEG
בחולה דמנציה המוגדר כחולה הנוטה למות מותר להמשיך הזנה פומית (COMFORT FEEDING ) ובמידת הצורך תוספת עירוי נוזלים
כדאי לדחות את התקנת ה PEG כמה שאפשר ולהשתמש בינתיים בזונדה, שכן פרוצדורת החדרת ה PEG הינה מורכבת
explanation:
התשובה הרשמית היא ג׳.

לפי המלצות המותב (עמ׳ 4–5), דרך הפה היא הדרך המועדפת למתן מזון ונוזלים; אם אינה מספקת, יש לשקול דרך חלופית לפי המצב הרפואי והוריות־הנגד של החולה המסוים.

**א. הארכת חיים מלאכותית בחולה נוטה למות הינה מנוגדת עקרונית לחוק ולכן לא מומלץ להאכיל בזונדה או PEG.** שגויה, אין איסור עקרוני כזה. ההמלצות מחייבות מזון ונוזלים גם באמצעים מלאכותיים בהיעדר הוריית נגד רפואית ברורה וספציפית בחולה המסוים (עמ׳ 5).
**ב. הדרך המועדפת להאכלה של חולים עם דמנציה סופנית הינה ב- PEG.** שגויה, העדיפות הראשונית היא להזנה דרך הפה. בחירת דרך חלופית נעשית לפי המצב הרפואי והיכולת להאכיל, ולכן אין המלצה אוטומטית ל-PEG לכל חולה (עמ׳ 5 עד 6).
**ג. בחולה דמנציה המוגדר כחולה הנוטה למות מותר להמשיך הזנה פומית (COMFORT FEEDING ) ובמידת הצורך תוספת עירוי נוזלים.** נכונה, זו התשובה הרשמית. ההמלצות מעדיפות מתן מזון ונוזלים דרך הפה, ואם אינו מספיק מחייבות לשקול דרך חלופית לפי צורכי החולה; עירוי הוא אחת האפשרויות, ולא פטור מהערכת ההזנה (עמ׳ 4 עד 6).
**ד. כדאי לדחות את התקנת ה PEG כמה שאפשר ולהשתמש בינתיים בזונדה, שכן פרוצדורת החדרת ה PEG הינה מורכבת.** שגויה, אין להחליף PEG בזונדה באופן קבוע בשל טענה כללית על מורכבות הפעולה. ההמלצות מציינות אי נוחות וסיבוכים של זונדה; דחייה קצרה של ההחלטה אפשרית לשם בירור רפואי תוך שמירת ההידרציה (עמ׳ 6).

**נקודת המפתח:** יש לתעד את ההחלטה ואת נימוקיה; ההמלצות אינן איסור גורף על הזנה מלאכותית (המלצות המותב, עמ׳ 5).

מקור: המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות, עמ׳ 4, 5, 6.
ref: המלצות ועד המותב — חוק החולה הנוטה למות

q: בת 87 אושפזה עקב אי ספיקת לב מתקדמת עם אנסרקה ותסמונת קרדיו-רנלית. סירבה דיאליזה ומבקשת לקבל טיפול פליאטיבי בלבד. מה העקרונות במתן טיפול הפליאטיבי בחולה זו?
o: טיפול תוך ורידי ב- FUSID IV אינו מוגדר כטיפול פליאטיבי
יש צורך בתישאול יומי לגבי קיום של עצירות
טיפול ב- MORPHINE טיפול הבחירה לכאבים
מעקב יומי של תפקודי כליה ואלקטרוליטים יעזור בבניית תכנית הטיפול
explanation:
In a patient receiving **palliative care** for advanced heart failure and cardiorenal syndrome, **monitoring constipation** is part of symptom management. Daily inquiry is the official answer, but that exact daily frequency is not specified on the checked source pages (Hazzard 8e, pp. 1071, 1074-1075).

**A. Intravenous FUSID is not palliative treatment.** Wrong, a diuretic for heart-failure-related breathlessness can relieve symptoms. Its route does not exclude it from palliative care (p. 1074; inference from treatment of the cause of dyspnea).
**B. Ask daily about constipation.** Correct, for official scoring. Symptom management and prevention of opioid-induced constipation are supported; the limitation concerning the exact daily frequency is preserved below (p. 1075).
**C. Morphine is the analgesic of choice.** Wrong, morphine is not a safe default in renal impairment: the described metabolite accumulates and may cause neurotoxicity, so the drug must be selected with renal function in mind (p. 1074).
**D. Daily renal function and electrolyte tests will help construct the treatment plan.** Wrong, a promise that daily testing will improve the plan does not follow from the patient's goals. Benefits and burdens should be weighed against her preferences rather than setting a uniform frequency from the diagnosis alone (p. 1075; inference from individualized treatment principles).

Official scoring accepts daily inquiry about constipation; the precise daily interval is not stated on the checked pages. Management of distressing symptoms is fundamental to palliative care (Hazzard 8e, pp. 1071, 1074-1075).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1071, 1074-1075.

q: בן 74, הסובל מ- COPD על רקע עישון כבד אובחן כסובל מ- NON SMALL CELL CARCINOMA של הריאה עם גרורות מרובות. הוא מאושפז במחלקה פנימית ומתלונן על קוצר נשימה. סטורציה 92%. מה עקרונות הטיפול הפליאטיבי בו?
o: מתן חמצן רק אם הסטורציה פחות מ- 90%
OXYCODONE היא תרופת הבחירה לקוצר נשימה
טכניקת הרפיה מועילה רק במידה וטיפול תרופתי נכשל
הנשמה לא פולשנית יכולה לעזור בהקלת הסימפטומים
explanation:
**Noninvasive ventilation** may relieve dyspnea. Weigh relief against anxiety and mask intolerance, guided by the patient's preferences (Hazzard 8e, pp. 1074-1075).

**A. Give oxygen only when saturation is below 90%.** Wrong, dyspnea treatment depends on cause, relief, and patient preferences; the source does not impose this single threshold on every palliative oxygen trial (pp. 1074-1075).
**B. Oxycodone is the drug of choice for dyspnea.** Wrong, the source discusses opioids for refractory dyspnea with attention to renal function and adverse effects; it does not identify oxycodone as the sole drug of choice (p. 1074).
**C. Relaxation is useful only after drug treatment fails.** Wrong, relaxation and breathing techniques are among initial approaches, so pharmacologic failure need not precede them (p. 1074).
**D. Noninvasive ventilation can relieve symptoms.** Correct, the study in advanced cancer showed dyspnea relief, with anxiety and mask intolerance to consider; selection depends on patient preferences (pp. 1074-1075).

Official IMA key: ד. IMA 2021-Dec Subspecialty official answer key, Q47. The conflicting bank explanation is hidden.

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1074-1075.

q: מה הייחוד של טיפול פליאטיבי בחולי דמנציה מטיפול פליאטיבי בחולים אונקולוגים?
o: בחולי דמנציה אין צורך בטיפול בכאב היות והשכיחות של כאב היא נמוכה
טיפול פליאטיבי בחולי דמנציה יכול התבצע בצורה טובה על ידי הצוות המטפל ואין חשיבות להכנסה של מומחים בטיפול פליאטיבי
חולי דמנציה מתקדמת סובלים מנטל סימפטומים גופניים משמעותי ובזה אינם שונים מחולים אונקולוגים
שילוב של טיפול פליאטיבי בחולי דמנציה חשוב רק בשלבים המתקדמים של המחלה
explanation:
Hazzard describes increasing **symptom burden in advanced dementia**, including pain, dysphagia, weight loss, and infections needing palliation (pp. 1047–1048). It also describes a high symptom burden in cancer (p. 1071). The inference supporting the official answer is that both populations have substantial physical symptoms, not that every symptom has identical frequency or severity.

**A. Patients with dementia do not need pain treatment because pain is uncommon.** Wrong, the source describes pain and the need to assess and relieve it in advanced dementia; inability to report it does not remove the need for treatment (p. 1048).
**B. The usual team can provide palliative care well, and specialist involvement is unimportant.** Wrong, primary palliative care belongs within usual care, but the source also includes referral to specialist teams when needed; dismissing their importance is unjustified (p. 1045).
**C. Advanced dementia has a substantial physical symptom burden, as does cancer.** Correct, officially accepted. The comparison concerns the existence of substantial burden, as explained in the source-based inference, not identity of every symptom (pp. 1047–1048, 1071).
**D. Palliative care matters only in advanced dementia.** Wrong, palliative care is appropriate at any stage of serious illness and can accompany disease treatment; it need not wait until advanced dementia (p. 1045).

**Official answer:** Patients with advanced dementia have a substantial physical symptom burden and in this respect do not differ from patients with cancer (IMA final answer key, December 2021, question 96).

The source-based comparison is an inference: significant physical symptom burden occurs in both groups; it does not establish identical symptom frequencies or intensities (Hazzard 8e, pp. 1047–1048, 1071).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1045, 1047–1048, 1071.

q: In the US framework described by Hazzard, how does a living will differ from a Physician Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST) form?
o: A living will records orders for current care; POLST records preferences for future care
A living will records preferences for future care; POLST records orders for current care
A living will appoints a health care proxy; POLST records preferences for future care
A living will records orders for current care; POLST appoints a health care proxy
explanation:
**Living wills** record wishes for future medical care if decision-making capacity is lost. **POLST** translates treatment preferences into a medical order for current care that accompanies the patient across care settings. (p. 1052)
"Allows a patient to specify in writing wishes for future medical care in the hypothetical situation where they lose decision-making capacity" (p. 1052)
"Standing medical order specifying decisions regarding current medical care for patients with progressive chronic illnesses" (p. 1052)

**A. A living will records orders for current care; POLST records preferences for future care.** Wrong, the living will concerns future wishes, while POLST contains orders for current treatment. (p. 1052)
**B. A living will records preferences for future care; POLST records orders for current care.** Correct, the distinction is between future treatment preferences and an actionable current medical order. (p. 1052)
**C. A living will appoints a health care proxy; POLST records preferences for future care.** Wrong, appointing a proxy is the function of a durable power of attorney for health care; POLST addresses current treatment. (p. 1052)
**D. A living will records orders for current care; POLST appoints a health care proxy.** Wrong, neither function is assigned correctly: living wills express future wishes, and POLST contains treatment orders rather than a proxy appointment. (p. 1052)

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., p. 1052.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A patient with advanced disease is about to discuss prognosis. Which opening step matches the communication approach described in Hazzard?
o: Give a numerical estimate before exploring the patient's wish for information
Explore current understanding and readiness to discuss the medical future
Avoid the discussion because it worsens depression and hopelessness
Give a definite estimate to reduce the uncertainty of the prognosis
explanation:
**Prognostic communication** begins with the patient's understanding and readiness. The information can then be tailored to what the patient wants and understands; prognostic estimates should still acknowledge their inherent uncertainty (pp. 1051-1052).
"it is first helpful to ask about the patient’s understanding of their illness and perception of what the future may have in store for them." (p. 1051).
"assess the readiness of the patient and/or family member to have a discussion of prognosis by asking them permission to talk about it." (p. 1051).

**A. Give a numerical estimate before exploring the patient's wish for information.** Wrong, the source first recommends exploring understanding and readiness, then tailoring the information rather than beginning with an unsolicited estimate (p. 1051).
**B. Explore current understanding and readiness to discuss the medical future.** Correct, this follows the source's initial assessment of understanding and permission to discuss prognosis (p. 1051).
**C. Avoid the discussion because it worsens depression and hopelessness.** Wrong, the source describes effective communication as beneficial without worsening anxiety, hopelessness, or depression; this proposed reason for avoidance is not supported (p. 1051).
**D. Give a definite estimate to reduce the uncertainty of the prognosis.** Wrong, the source recommends acknowledging uncertainty, rather than presenting an estimate as definite (p. 1052).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1051, 1052.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: When assessing eligibility for the Medicare hospice benefit in the United States, what central clinical consideration must the attending physician and hospice medical director certify, according to Hazzard?
o: Dependence on help with activities of daily living at home
Terminal illness with an expected short prognosis
New weight loss during the current hospital admission
A need for continuous nursing care in the home
explanation:
**Hospice eligibility depends on prognosis certification.** Hazzard describes certification of terminal illness with an expected prognosis of less than six months if the disease follows its usual course (p. 1046). The deciding wording is "terminally ill with an expected prognosis of less than 6 months" (p. 1046).

**A. Dependence on help with activities of daily living at home.** Wrong, functional dependence alone is not the prognosis certification specified by the source (p. 1046).
**B. Terminal illness with an expected short prognosis.** Correct, this describes the required terminal-illness and prognosis judgment (p. 1046).
**C. New weight loss during the current hospital admission.** Wrong, weight loss alone does not establish the stated prognosis criterion (p. 1046).
**D. A need for continuous nursing care in the home.** Wrong, nursing needs alone do not establish the terminal prognosis that must be certified (p. 1046).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1046.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A patient with advanced dementia (FAST 7c) develops aspiration pneumonia. Which statement best describes the evidence summarized in Hazzard?
o: Antibiotics are associated with longer survival but not improved comfort; treatment should reflect goals of care
Antibiotics are associated with improved comfort more than survival; treatment primarily relieves suffering
Intravenous antibiotics and hospitalization provide greater survival benefit than other administration routes
Advanced dementia prevents a survival benefit from antibiotics; treatment does not serve life-prolongation goals
explanation:
**Antibiotics for aspiration pneumonia** in advanced dementia have been associated with improved survival but not improved comfort. The source reports similar survival benefit across routes, with greatest discomfort from intravenous treatment and hospitalization, so goals of care matter (p. 1048).
"Antibiotic therapy for aspiration pneumonia in advanced dementia has been associated with improved survival but not improved comfort." (p. 1048).

**A. Antibiotics are associated with longer survival but not improved comfort; treatment should reflect goals of care.** Correct, this preserves the distinction between survival and comfort and applies the source's goals-based approach (p. 1048).
**B. Antibiotics are associated with improved comfort more than survival; treatment primarily relieves suffering.** Wrong, the reported association is improved survival without improved comfort, not primarily comfort improvement (p. 1048).
**C. Intravenous antibiotics and hospitalization provide greater survival benefit than other administration routes.** Wrong, survival benefit was similar regardless of route; the most aggressive approaches were associated with greatest discomfort (p. 1048).
**D. Advanced dementia prevents a survival benefit from antibiotics; treatment does not serve life-prolongation goals.** Wrong, the source reports an association with improved survival in advanced dementia, so dementia does not support the claimed absence of benefit (p. 1048).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1048.

q: מהו Death Rattle ומהו הטיפול?
o: רעש נשימתי מהצטברות הפרשות בדרכי אוויר בחולה גוסס; טיפול: Hyoscine (Scopolamine) או Glycopyrrolate
סימן לדלקת ריאות הדורש אנטיביוטיקה
סימן לאסתמה
סימן לכשל לבבי חריף
explanation:
**Death rattle מתרחש ב-23-92% מהגוססים**.

**א. רעש נשימתי מהצטברות הפרשות בדרכי אוויר בחולה גוסס; טיפול: Hyoscine (Scopolamine) או Glycopyrrolate.** נכונה, נגרם מחוסר יכולת לפנות הפרשות. Anticholinergics (Hyoscine butylbromide 20mg SC, Glycopyrrolate 0.2mg SC) מפחיתים ייצור הפרשות. שאיבה לא מומלצת — גורמת אי-נוחות. חשוב להסביר למשפחה שהמטופל אינו סובל.
**ב. סימן לדלקת ריאות הדורש אנטיביוטיקה.** שגויה.
**ג. סימן לאסתמה.** שגויה.
**ד. סימן לכשל לבבי חריף.** שגויה.

מקור: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A 72-year-old woman with metastatic breast cancer diagnosed six months ago has worsening fatigue, reduced appetite, and mild dyspnea over a month. Chemotherapy is controlling the disease, but her ECOG performance status has declined from 1 to 2. Her daughter is concerned about quality of life. Alongside assessment of the new symptoms, which approach to palliative care is supported by Hazzard?
o: Introduce palliative care alongside the ongoing oncology treatment
Postpone palliative care until chemotherapy has been discontinued
Postpone palliative care until progression is shown on imaging
Postpone palliative care until a terminal prognosis is certified
explanation:
**Palliative care can accompany active cancer treatment.** It addresses symptom burden and stress for the patient and family and does not require stopping curative or disease-directed care (p. 1045). "It is appropriate for any type of diagnosis, any stage of a serious illness, and importantly, can be provided together with curative treatment." (p. 1045).

**A. Introduce palliative care alongside the ongoing oncology treatment.** Correct, concurrent palliative and oncology care matches the source definition (p. 1045).
**B. Postpone palliative care until chemotherapy has been discontinued.** Wrong, the source permits concurrent treatment rather than requiring chemotherapy discontinuation (p. 1045).
**C. Postpone palliative care until progression is shown on imaging.** Wrong, the definition does not make radiographic progression a prerequisite; it applies at any stage of serious illness (p. 1045).
**D. Postpone palliative care until a terminal prognosis is certified.** Wrong, a terminal prognosis is not required for palliative care at any stage of serious illness (p. 1045).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1045.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An 85-year-old woman in the United States has metastatic breast cancer. Palliative chemotherapy initially helped, but after eight months she has increasing fatigue, two recent falls, and a decline in ECOG performance status from 2 to 3. She wishes to stop chemotherapy, prioritize comfort, and remain at home. Her physicians certify a prognosis of less than six months if the disease follows its expected course. Which plan best matches her stated goals?
o: Continue the current chemotherapy and add fall-focused physical therapy
Arrange hospice care focused on comfort and support at home
Change to another chemotherapy regimen with a lower treatment burden
Increase palliative visits while continuing the current chemotherapy
explanation:
**Hospice** provides comfort and support for patients nearing the end of life and their families. The stem supplies both the prognostic certification required for Medicare hospice and the patient's preference for comfort-focused care, rather than inferring eligibility from performance status alone (pp. 1045–1046). "Hospice care does not aim to shorten or prolong life, but rather provides comfort and support services" (p. 1045).

**A. Continue the current chemotherapy and add fall-focused physical therapy.** Wrong, this retains chemotherapy despite the explicitly stated preference to stop it and prioritize comfort (p. 1045).
**B. Arrange hospice care focused on comfort and support at home.** Correct, hospice's comfort and support focus matches the stated goals, with the required prognostic certification supplied (pp. 1045–1046).
**C. Change to another chemotherapy regimen with a lower treatment burden.** Wrong, switching regimens continues cancer-directed treatment that the patient has said she wishes to stop (p. 1045).
**D. Increase palliative visits while continuing the current chemotherapy.** Wrong, palliative involvement is compatible with many treatment plans, but this option still continues the chemotherapy she has declined (p. 1045).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1045, 1046.

q: אישה בת 91 עם COPD מתקדם על חמצן ביתי, אוסטאופורוזיס עם multiple compression fractures, וכאב כרוני — מוערכת על ידי צוות CGA האשפוזי בשל failure to thrive. היא שוקלת 82 פאונד (BMI 16) וזקוקה לעזרה בכל ה-ADLs. היא אומרת לצוות שהיא 'מוכנה ללכת' ורוצה להפסיק את כל התרופות מלבד טיפול בכאב. בתה מתעקשת על 'לעשות הכל' כולל האכלה בזונדה. כיצד על צוות ה-CGA להמשיך?
o: לכבד את רצון הבת כ-next-of-kin
להזמין consult פסיכיאטרי להערכת capacity
לתעד את רצון המטופלת ולהפנות ל-hospice
לפנות לוועדת האתיקה להכוונה
explanation:
**בירור ותיעוד רצון המטופלת** הם הבסיס להתאמת הטיפול, כאשר נמסר לה מידע המאפשר החלטה מרצון והבנה (חוק זכויות החולה, סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8). בקשה להתמקד בהקלה אינה כשלעצמה הוכחה לחוסר יכולת לקבל החלטות; יש להעריך את ההבנה והמשמעות האישית של הבחירה בשיחה קלינית (Hazzard, עמ׳ 151, 154). כהסקה מן המחלה המתקדמת והתלות המתוארות, אפשר להפנות להערכת הוספיס בהתאם למטרותיה, אך עצם הירידה בתפקוד אינה קובעת זכאות או פרוגנוזה סופנית (עמ׳ 1045–1046, 1049).
"Hospice care is a specialized form of palliative care for patients with limited life expectancy." (עמ׳ 1045).

**א. לכבד את רצון הבת כ-next-of-kin.** שגויה, קרבה משפחתית אינה סיבה להתעלם מן המטופלת ולהחליף את רצונה ברצון הבת. יש לברר עמה את הטיפול והחלופות באופן המאפשר החלטה מדעת (עמ׳ חוק זכויות החולה, 8, סעיף 13).
**ב. להזמין consult פסיכיאטרי להערכת capacity.** שגויה, יש לבדוק את יכולת קבלת ההחלטות, אך אין בתיאור לבדו בסיס להפניה אוטומטית לפסיכיאטר. הספר מתאר שיחה קלינית מתועדת הבוחנת הבנה, הערכה ושיקול דעת (עמ׳ 151, 154).
**ג. לתעד את רצון המטופלת ולהפנות ל-hospice.** נכונה, תיעוד המטרות והפניה להערכה מתאימים לבקשה להקל על הסבל במחלה מתקדמת. יש להשלים הערכה פרטנית של פרוגנוזה וצרכים לפני קביעה שהיא מתאימה למסגרת הוספיס (עמ׳ 1045–1046, 1049).
**ד. לפנות לוועדת האתיקה להכוונה.** שגויה, ייעוץ נוסף עשוי לעזור במחלוקת שאינה נפתרת, אך אינו מחליף את הבירור הישיר של רצון המטופלת ויכולתה להחליט. כהסקה מהתיאור, אין סיבה לדלג על בירור ותיעוד אלה (עמ׳ 154; חוק זכויות החולה, 8, סעיף 13).

מקור: חוק זכויות החולה, סעיף 13, עמ׳ 8 בעותק המקור; Hazzard 8e, עמ׳ 151, 154, 1045–1046, 1049.

q: An 86-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced Parkinson disease is hospitalized with aspiration pneumonia. She is bedbound, needs a pureed diet, and has lost 15 lb over three months. She takes carbidopa–levodopa, quetiapine 25 mg at bedtime for hallucinations, and mirtazapine 15 mg for depression; creatinine clearance is 32 mL/min. After stabilization, her daughter asks about tube feeding. The patient and family choose comfort-focused care, and the attending physician and hospice medical director certify a terminal prognosis of less than six months if the illness follows its expected course. Which service model fits these established goals and eligibility?
o: Hospice care for interdisciplinary symptom relief and family support
Rehabilitation care directed at achieving an intensive daily therapy target
Disease-focused care directed at prolonging life as its primary outcome
Procedural care directed at tube placement before discussing care goals
explanation:
**Hospice** provides comfort and support to people with limited life expectancy and supports their families (pp. 1045–1046). "Hospice care does not aim to shorten or prolong life, but rather provides comfort and support services" (p. 1045). The additional prognosis certification in this stem establishes the Medicare eligibility element described by the source (p. 1046).

**A. Hospice care for interdisciplinary symptom relief and family support.** Correct, this matches the established comfort goals and prognosis certification (pp. 1045–1046).
**B. Rehabilitation care directed at achieving an intensive daily therapy target.** Wrong, an intensive rehabilitation target does not express the hospice comfort-and-support model selected in this stem (p. 1045).
**C. Disease-focused care directed at prolonging life as its primary outcome.** Wrong, the source distinguishes hospice from a model aimed at prolonging life (p. 1045).
**D. Procedural care directed at tube placement before discussing care goals.** Wrong, palliative care aligns treatment with goals through communication; choosing a procedure before that discussion does not reflect this approach (p. 1045).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1045, 1046.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An 83-year-old man with advanced heart and lung disease wants relief of breathlessness and distress. His daughter worries that adding palliative care means abandoning disease treatment. Which explanation matches the source definition?
o: Palliative care starts at the final stage after curative treatment ends
Palliative care makes prolonging life the primary goal of its plan
Palliative care relieves symptoms alongside disease treatment and patient goals
Palliative care makes normalization of disease measurements its central goal
explanation:
**Palliative care** focuses on relief of symptoms, pain, and stress and on care that matches the patient’s goals (p. 1045). It is not confined to the end of life: "It is appropriate for any type of diagnosis, any stage of a serious illness, and importantly, can be provided together with curative treatment." (p. 1045).

**A. Palliative care starts at the final stage after curative treatment ends.** Wrong, the source permits palliative care at any stage and alongside curative treatment (p. 1045).
**B. Palliative care makes prolonging life the primary goal of its plan.** Wrong, the definition emphasizes quality of life and symptom relief, with goals individualized rather than fixed on life prolongation (p. 1045).
**C. Palliative care relieves symptoms alongside disease treatment and patient goals.** Correct, this reflects concurrent symptom relief and goal-concordant disease care (p. 1045).
**D. Palliative care makes normalization of disease measurements its central goal.** Wrong, the source centers symptoms, quality of life, and patient goals rather than normalization of disease measurements (p. 1045).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1045.

q: A 77-year-old man with heart failure and multimorbidity has stabilized after hospitalization but continues to have symptoms and treatment burden. A palliative care consultation is being considered. Which description of its role matches Hazzard?
o: Improve quality of life and relieve symptoms alongside disease treatment
Replace disease treatment after determining that the illness is terminal
Defer symptom treatment until a decision is made to stop curative care
Shorten the remaining lifespan as the central purpose of supportive care
explanation:
**Palliative care** aims to improve quality of life and relieve the symptoms, pain and stress of serious illness. It is appropriate at any stage and can accompany curative treatment; it therefore need not wait for a terminal-stage decision (p. 1045).
"Palliative care aims to improve the quality of life for both the patient with serious illness and the family." (p. 1045).
"It is appropriate for any type of diagnosis, any stage of a serious illness, and importantly, can be provided together with curative treatment." (p. 1045).

**A. Improve quality of life and relieve symptoms alongside disease treatment.** Correct, this combines the stated aims of symptom relief and quality of life with the ability to continue disease-directed treatment (p. 1045).
**B. Replace disease treatment after determining that the illness is terminal.** Wrong, the source allows palliative care at any stage together with curative treatment, rather than defining it as replacement after a terminal diagnosis (p. 1045).
**C. Defer symptom treatment until a decision is made to stop curative care.** Wrong, symptom relief is a core purpose and is compatible with continued curative treatment (p. 1045).
**D. Shorten the remaining lifespan as the central purpose of supportive care.** Wrong, the described purpose is quality of life and relief of suffering; even hospice is stated not to aim at shortening or prolonging life (p. 1045).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1045.

q: An 82-year-old woman with advanced heart failure and recurrent admissions says that remaining at home matters to her. The team starts a goals-of-care and advance care planning conversation. What is the central purpose of this process?
o: Create a plan organized around the usual life-prolongation target for heart failure
Create a plan implementing the full drug protocol for each separate chronic disease
Create a plan aligning treatments with her values and preferences
Create a plan delivering the greatest treatment intensity available in her home
explanation:
**Advance care planning** supports understanding and sharing personal values, goals and preferences for future care. Its focus is a meaningful conversation that aligns the recommended treatments with the patient, and the process should continue as priorities change (p. 1052).
"The focus of ACP is on meaningful conversations in order to create a care plan that aligns recommended treatments with patient preferences." (p. 1052).
"ACP should be ongoing as the values or priorities of people may change as they go through life" (p. 1052).

**A. Create a plan organized around the usual life-prolongation target for heart failure.** Wrong, a standard disease-based target cannot substitute for the stated purpose of aligning treatment with individual preferences (p. 1052).
**B. Create a plan implementing the full drug protocol for each separate chronic disease.** Wrong, implementing separate disease protocols does not itself establish alignment with the preferences and goals being discussed (p. 1052).
**C. Create a plan aligning treatments with her values and preferences.** Correct, this is the purpose the source assigns to advance care planning (p. 1052).
**D. Create a plan delivering the greatest treatment intensity available in her home.** Wrong, available treatment intensity is not the organizing goal; the source calls for a plan aligned with patient preferences (p. 1052).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1052.

q: An 82-year-old man with hip osteoarthritis and early frailty is referred for prehabilitation before surgery. Inadequate nutritional intake is also identified. Which program is consistent with Hazzard's approach to early frailty?
o: Correct nutritional inadequacy and incorporate resistance exercise
Correct nutritional inadequacy and postpone exercise until surgery
Reduce physical activity and conserve energy for recovery
Reduce daily activity and rely on prolonged periods of rest
explanation:
**Early frailty management** combines nutritional care with resistance or strengthening exercise. The table describes benefits for muscle mass, strength and walking speed, and includes prehabilitation before surgery (p. 1049).
"Encourage resistance and strength exercise." (p. 1049).

**A. Correct nutritional inadequacy and incorporate resistance exercise.** Correct, this combines nutritional correction with the exercise component recommended for early frailty (p. 1049).
**B. Correct nutritional inadequacy and postpone exercise until surgery.** Wrong, postponing exercise omits a recommended intervention; the table says nutritional supplementation appears effective when added to resistance exercise (p. 1049).
**C. Reduce physical activity and conserve energy for recovery.** Wrong, the preventive measures carried into early-frailty care aim to maintain activity and minimize immobility (p. 1049).
**D. Reduce daily activity and rely on prolonged periods of rest.** Wrong, prolonged rest conflicts with maintaining activity and encouraging strength and resistance exercise (p. 1049).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1049.

q: A woman with dementia and a painful fracture continues to show signs of pain despite an adequate trial of acetaminophen. What can be considered next under the stepwise pain-treatment approach described in Hazzard?
o: Consider an antipsychotic as the initial treatment for persistent pain
Consider waiting for a detailed verbal report before changing treatment
Consider discontinuing analgesics because the patient has a dementia diagnosis
Consider an opioid trial while assessing the patient’s response
explanation:
An empiric **stepwise pain protocol** in patients with dementia starts with acetaminophen and allows an opioid trial for nonresponders. Hazzard states: "Most patients were treated with the first step of the protocol, acetaminophen. Opioids may be tried for nonresponders." (p. 1048).

**A. Consider an antipsychotic as the initial treatment for persistent pain.** Wrong, the pain protocol proceeds from acetaminophen to an opioid trial for nonresponders; it does not identify an antipsychotic as the next analgesic step (p. 1048).
**B. Consider waiting for a detailed verbal report before changing treatment.** Wrong, the source describes empiric pain treatment and a possible role for the PAINAD scale, rather than requiring a detailed verbal account before addressing persistent pain (p. 1048).
**C. Consider discontinuing analgesics because the patient has a dementia diagnosis.** Wrong, the protocol treats pain in patients with dementia and offers an opioid trial after nonresponse, rather than stopping analgesia because of the diagnosis (p. 1048).
**D. Consider an opioid trial while assessing the patient’s response.** Correct, persistent pain after an acetaminophen trial fits the nonresponse for which the source permits an opioid trial (p. 1048).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1048.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An 84-year-old transgender woman with COPD, frailty (CFS 6), and depression is hospitalized with pneumonia. She transitioned three years ago and is estranged from her biological family. Her chosen family of LGBTQ friends visits, but hospital security questions their status as family. She withdraws from participation in care. Which response follows Hazzard's guidance on families of choice?
o: Recognize her biological relatives as family and classify her chosen supporters as visitors.
Ask the care team to define her family membership before including her chosen supporters.
Respect her chosen supporters as family and advocate for their inclusion in her care.
Require her relatives to confirm family membership before including her chosen supporters.
explanation:
**Families of choice** are to be respected as family according to the patient's identification. Estrangement from biological relatives can make close friends important caregivers (p. 1050). "Informal communities of support are also known as “lavender families” or “families of choice” and should be respected and included as family as identified by patients." (p. 1050).

**A. Recognize her biological relatives as family and classify her chosen supporters as visitors.** Wrong, this substitutes biological relationship for the patient-defined family described in the source (p. 1050).
**B. Ask the care team to define her family membership before including her chosen supporters.** Wrong, the source assigns family identification to the patient, not to the care team (p. 1050).
**C. Respect her chosen supporters as family and advocate for their inclusion in her care.** Correct, respecting and including the family she identifies applies the stated guidance to the barrier described (p. 1050).
**D. Require her relatives to confirm family membership before including her chosen supporters.** Wrong, requiring relatives to approve substitutes their definition for the patient's identification (p. 1050).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1050.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A 91-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease, dysphagia and recurrent aspiration pneumonia is brought by his son for a goals-of-care discussion. He has lost 15 pounds in 3 months, sleeps 18 hours a day and needs full assistance with activities of daily living. His son insists on a PEG tube, saying, "I cannot let Dad starve." The patient previously expressed a wish to avoid tubes and machines. Which response best begins this conversation?
o: Let us review feeding-tube outcomes and then ask what you expect from treatment.
Let us finalize the plan from his previous wishes and then discuss your concerns.
Let us discuss your understanding of his illness and then explore his priorities for care.
Let us decide about tube placement and then discuss his goals and preferences.
explanation:
**Understanding and patient priorities** guide a goals-of-care conversation before a treatment recommendation. Hazzard advises that "it is first helpful to ask about the patient’s understanding of their illness and perception of what the future may have in store for them." (p. 1051). It also states: "The focus of ACP is on meaningful conversations in order to create a care plan that aligns recommended treatments with patient preferences." (p. 1052). Inference: applying these principles to the son's request means exploring his understanding and the father's priorities before settling the feeding-tube plan; these pages do not establish a Parkinson-specific rule against PEG.

**A. Let us review feeding-tube outcomes and then ask what you expect from treatment.** Wrong, this sequence presents treatment information before asking about expectations. Inference: it misses the source's suggested starting point of understanding the person's current view so that information can be tailored to it (p. 1051).
**B. Let us finalize the plan from his previous wishes and then discuss your concerns.** Wrong, this sequence finalizes the plan before exploring the son's concerns. Inference: the father's previous preferences remain relevant, but using them to close the discussion first bypasses the meaningful conversation that connects recommendations with patient preferences (pp. 1051–1052).
**C. Let us discuss your understanding of his illness and then explore his priorities for care.** Correct, this sequence explores understanding and patient priorities before a treatment decision. Inference: it applies the source's communication and advance-care-planning principles to the son while preserving attention to the father's wishes (pp. 1051–1052).
**D. Let us decide about tube placement and then discuss his goals and preferences.** Wrong, this sequence makes the tube decision before discussing goals and preferences. Inference: it reverses the source's process of using the conversation to create a care plan aligned with those preferences (p. 1052).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., chapter 67, pp. 1051–1052 (PDF pp. 1085–1086).

q: A 76-year-old woman with advanced cancer expresses fear of death and asks to talk about the future. How does Hazzard recommend opening the prognosis discussion?
o: Assess her understanding and readiness, then tailor the information to her
Present the full survival details before assessing her understanding of the illness
Postpone discussion because it is expected to worsen anxiety and hopelessness
Set the content according to family wishes without assessing her own preferences
explanation:
**Prognosis communication** begins by assessing the patient’s understanding and readiness for discussion. The chapter recommends information "tailored to the patient’s current desire and level of understanding" and describes evidence of benefit without worsening anxiety, hopelessness, or depression (p. 1051).

**A. Assess her understanding and readiness, then tailor the information to her.** Correct, understanding and readiness guide how much prognostic information to share and how to frame it (p. 1051).
**B. Present the full survival details before assessing her understanding of the illness.** Wrong, delivering all details first bypasses the recommended assessment that allows the information to be tailored (p. 1051).
**C. Postpone discussion because it is expected to worsen anxiety and hopelessness.** Wrong, the chapter describes benefit from effective end-of-life communication without worsening anxiety or hopelessness, so this presumed harm does not justify postponement (p. 1051).
**D. Set the content according to family wishes without assessing her own preferences.** Wrong, the patient’s own desire and understanding are part of tailoring the discussion; family preferences do not replace that assessment (p. 1051).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 1051.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An 83-year-old man with heart failure, stage 3b CKD (eGFR 35), and mild dementia is receiving hospice care for end-stage heart disease. Severe peripheral edema is causing skin breakdown and discomfort. He takes morphine 5 mg every four hours and metoprolol 25 mg twice daily. His wife asks whether a diuretic could help. Which approach follows the source treatment of symptomatic congestion?
o: Start furosemide with monitoring and adjustment to the response
Avoid diuretics because they conflict with hospice symptom goals
Start metolazone before trying a loop diuretic for congestion
Use spironolactone as a more potent diuretic than furosemide
explanation:
**Diuretics can relieve symptomatic congestion**, a goal consistent with hospice comfort care. Loop diuretics are widely used; monitoring is important because older adults are vulnerable to electrolyte abnormalities during titration (pp. 1045, 1182). "Diuretics are the most effective agents for relieving pulmonary congestion and edema" (p. 1182).

**A. Start furosemide with monitoring and adjustment to the response.** Correct, furosemide is a loop diuretic directed at congestion and edema; monitoring and titration follow the source approach (p. 1182).
**B. Avoid diuretics because they conflict with hospice symptom goals.** Wrong, hospice provides comfort and support, so a treatment directed at distressing edema is consistent with that goal (pp. 1045, 1182; application to this case).
**C. Start metolazone before trying a loop diuretic for congestion.** Wrong, metolazone is described as an addition when response to a loop diuretic is inadequate, not the initial substitution proposed here (p. 1182).
**D. Use spironolactone as a more potent diuretic than furosemide.** Wrong, spironolactone is described as a relatively weak diuretic; the proposed potency comparison is incorrect (pp. 1181–1182).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1045, 1181, 1182.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A care-home resident with dementia and behavioral problems is assessed for possible pain. What was the first step in the empiric stepwise pain-treatment protocol described in Hazzard?
o: Begin an initial therapeutic trial of acetaminophen
Begin an initial therapeutic trial of an antipsychotic
Begin an initial therapeutic trial of an opioid
Wait for a detailed verbal description of the pain
explanation:
**Pain treatment in dementia** can be approached empirically when behavioral symptoms raise concern for pain. In the nursing-home trial described by Hazzard, the first step was acetaminophen; opioids were an option for nonresponders, and antipsychotics were not recommended as first-line treatment for behavioral symptoms (p. 1048).
"Most patients were treated with the first step of the protocol, acetaminophen." (p. 1048).

**A. Begin an initial therapeutic trial of acetaminophen.** Correct, acetaminophen was the initial step in the protocol, and most patients in the trial were treated at that step (p. 1048).
**B. Begin an initial therapeutic trial of an antipsychotic.** Wrong, the source recommends against antipsychotics as first-line treatment for behavioral and psychological symptoms of dementia and identifies acetaminophen as the first pain-treatment step (p. 1048).
**C. Begin an initial therapeutic trial of an opioid.** Wrong, opioids were considered for patients who did not respond, rather than as the initial step (p. 1048).
**D. Wait for a detailed verbal description of the pain.** Wrong, the described approach is an empiric pain-treatment protocol and also mentions PAINAD as an assessment aid; a detailed verbal report is not the stated first step (p. 1048).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1048.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A 76-year-old man with COPD on home oxygen, heart failure (EF 25%), and stage 3b CKD has worsening dyspnea over several months despite optimized disease-directed treatment. He is homebound and uses a walker for short distances. His wife provides round-the-clock care and appears exhausted. He asks about hospice but says, “I am not ready to give up.” Which response best explains an available approach?
o: Provide home palliative care alongside ongoing treatment of his illnesses
Palliative care should follow withdrawal of disease-directed treatment
Palliative care referral should await a prognosis shorter than six months
Symptom management should be completed before discussing care goals
explanation:
**Palliative care** can address symptoms and family needs alongside disease-directed treatment. Hazzard says it is appropriate at any stage of serious illness and “can be provided together with curative treatment” (p. 1045). Home-based models include symptom management, goals discussions, and caregiver support; they do not require an all-or-nothing choice between those services and treating his illnesses (p. 1084).

**A. Provide home palliative care alongside ongoing treatment of his illnesses.** Correct, concurrent care is explicitly supported, and home-based palliative services address the symptom and caregiver needs described (pp. 1045, 1084).
**B. Palliative care should follow withdrawal of disease-directed treatment.** Wrong, requiring withdrawal contradicts the source’s concurrent-treatment model (p. 1045).
**C. Palliative care referral should await a prognosis shorter than six months.** Wrong, the six-month prognosis criterion concerns the Medicare hospice benefit, not palliative care at any stage of serious illness (pp. 1045–1046).
**D. Symptom management should be completed before discussing care goals.** Wrong, the source combines symptom management and goals discussions within palliative care rather than making completion of one a prerequisite for the other (pp. 1045, 1084).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1045, 1084, 1046.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A 79-year-old woman with advanced heart failure asks about life expectancy so that she can plan. Her physician has a prognostic estimate but substantial uncertainty remains for the individual. How should it be communicated?
o: Present the group mean as her personal survival date for planning
Postpone prognostic details until an exact survival date can be given
Present a range or scenarios and explain the uncertainty
Focus on symptoms to reduce the need to discuss expected survival
explanation:
**Prognostic communication** should acknowledge uncertainty rather than turn a population estimate into a fixed individual date. Hazzard suggests ranges or best-case, worst-case, and most-common scenarios to communicate an estimate honestly (p. 1052). "When delivering prognostic estimates, clinicians should acknowledge the inherent uncertainty in most prognostic estimates." (p. 1052).

**A. Present the group mean as her personal survival date for planning.** Wrong, a fixed personal date from a group mean hides the inherent uncertainty the source says to acknowledge (p. 1052).
**B. Postpone prognostic details until an exact survival date can be given.** Wrong, the source gives ways to communicate estimates despite uncertainty; an exact date is not required before discussion (p. 1052).
**C. Present a range or scenarios and explain the uncertainty.** Correct, ranges and scenarios are the methods suggested for expressing the uncertainty in prognostic estimates (p. 1052).
**D. Focus on symptoms to reduce the need to discuss expected survival.** Wrong, discussing symptoms instead does not answer her request; the source describes communicating prognosis with explicit uncertainty (p. 1052).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1052.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An 85-year-old woman with severe COPD (FEV1 22%), osteoporosis, and severe frailty (CFS 7) lives alone with daily home help. She is hospitalized with influenza and respiratory failure requiring BiPAP. After recovery, she wants to return home and understands the risks, although the team is concerned about safety. Which plan combines her goal with the source approach to advanced COPD and diminished abilities?
o: Return home with prior services and defer reassessment of support needs
Move to residential care and defer discussion of her preference for home
Return home and discontinue COPD treatments when palliative care begins
Return home with palliative care and support matched to her needs
explanation:
**Palliative care in advanced COPD** aims to relieve symptoms while maintaining independence and dignity. Severe frailty calls for adapting the environment or increasing caregiver support; applying both principles supports a home plan tailored to her assessed needs (pp. 1049, 1262). "Compensate for diminished abilities by modification of living environment and/or increased support from caregivers." (p. 1049).

**A. Return home with prior services and defer reassessment of support needs.** Wrong, leaving support unchanged without reassessment does not address the source recommendation to compensate for diminished abilities (p. 1049).
**B. Move to residential care and defer discussion of her preference for home.** Wrong, a plan made before discussing her preference does not follow the goal-based approach of optimizing abilities needed to reach individual goals (p. 1049).
**C. Return home and discontinue COPD treatments when palliative care begins.** Wrong, palliative COPD care includes continuation of appropriate symptom-relieving pulmonary treatments; it does not require their discontinuation (p. 1262).
**D. Return home with palliative care and support matched to her needs.** Correct, it integrates the patient's goal with symptom care and practical support; actual arrangements must follow assessment of her abilities and needs (pp. 1049, 1262; case application).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1049, 1262.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A woman with advanced illness requests a survival estimate to plan her affairs. When a clinical estimate is available, how does Hazzard recommend communicating it?
o: Provide a precise date and narrow the discussion of possible outcomes
Provide a range and acknowledge uncertainty in the estimate
Emphasize an optimistic point estimate when describing expected survival
Provide a numerical estimate and set aside the emotional response
explanation:
**Prognostic estimates** should be communicated with acknowledgement of uncertainty. A range or discussion of best, worst, and most common scenarios is one way to convey this; emotional responses also warrant support (p. 1052). "When delivering prognostic estimates, clinicians should acknowledge the inherent uncertainty in most prognostic estimates." (p. 1052).

**A. Provide a precise date and narrow the discussion of possible outcomes.** Wrong, a precise date with narrowed discussion fails to convey the uncertainty the source recommends acknowledging (p. 1052).
**B. Provide a range and acknowledge uncertainty in the estimate.** Correct, a range is an explicitly suggested way to communicate the uncertainty of a prognostic estimate (p. 1052).
**C. Emphasize an optimistic point estimate when describing expected survival.** Wrong, emphasizing an optimistic point estimate does not convey the range or the best, worst, and most common scenarios described in the source (p. 1052).
**D. Provide a numerical estimate and set aside the emotional response.** Wrong, the source recognizes likely emotional reactions and recommends empathic support, rather than setting those reactions aside (p. 1052).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1052.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES
chapterTitle: PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An 80-year-old woman with heart failure, chronic kidney disease and newly diagnosed lung adenocarcinoma is hospitalized with decompensated heart failure. The oncologist recommends pembrolizumab, while the cardiologist is concerned about cardiac toxicity. She lives independently and manages her instrumental activities. She says, "I want to fight the cancer, but I also want to be at home with my grandchildren." What should the team clarify to align the treatment plan with her priorities?
o: The most intensive cancer treatment supported by a disease-specific protocol
The competing illness that should determine care before exploring her goals
The treatment to select from functional status before discussing her goals
Her priorities for time at home and quality of life
explanation:
**Individual goals of care** guide the balancing of life prolongation, function, treatment harm and symptom relief. Palliative care aims to match individualized care plans to those goals; clarifying the meaning of the patient's stated priorities supports that task without declaring a specific cancer treatment beneficial or futile (p. 1045).
"balancing: goals of life prolongation, functional status preservation and restoration, risk and harm mitigation, and symptom relief." (p. 1045).
"Palliative care aims to ensure that these goals match the individualized care plans through interprofessional care and careful communication and goal setting." (p. 1045).

**A. The most intensive cancer treatment supported by a disease-specific protocol.** Wrong, treatment intensity by itself does not establish whether a plan matches the patient's goals (p. 1045).
**B. The competing illness that should determine care before exploring her goals.** Wrong, selecting a dominant illness before exploring her priorities bypasses the goal-setting process described (p. 1045).
**C. The treatment to select from functional status before discussing her goals.** Wrong, functional status is relevant, but the source calls for balancing multiple goals and harms rather than deciding from function alone (p. 1045).
**D. Her priorities for time at home and quality of life.** Correct, this clarifies the patient's own priorities so the individualized plan can balance them with benefits and burdens (p. 1045).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 1045.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: An 86-year-old man with severe aortic stenosis, stage 3b CKD, and frailty (CFS 6) is offered TAVR. He uses a wheelchair, needs help with all IADLs, and receives continuous care from his wife. He wants comfort and to die at home when the time comes. His cardiologist emphasizes possible life prolongation; his wife is uncertain. What should the team do next?
o: Advance the TAVR plan based on stenosis severity before discussing his preferences
Arrange palliative care input to clarify goals before deciding about the procedure
Arrange direct hospice enrollment based on frailty before discussing procedural benefit
Attribute the comfort preference to depression and defer discussion for psychiatric review
explanation:
**Goals-of-care discussion** aligns proposed treatments with patient preferences rather than equating a diagnosis with a predetermined plan (p. 1052). The source describes "meaningful conversations in order to create a care plan that aligns recommended treatments with patient preferences" (p. 1052).

**A. Advance the TAVR plan based on stenosis severity before discussing his preferences.** Wrong, proceeding from stenosis severity without eliciting preferences omits the alignment required by the source (p. 1052).
**B. Arrange palliative care input to clarify goals before deciding about the procedure.** Correct, clarifying goals creates the basis for assessing whether the proposed procedure fits what he values (p. 1052).
**C. Arrange direct hospice enrollment based on frailty before discussing procedural benefit.** Wrong, direct hospice enrollment before discussing benefits and preferences also predetermines the plan rather than aligning it with informed goals (p. 1052).
**D. Attribute the comfort preference to depression and defer discussion for psychiatric review.** Wrong, a stated comfort preference is information for the goals discussion; assigning depression from that preference is not established by the stem or source (p. 1052; application).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1052.

q: An 88-year-old man with dementia and aortic stenosis is being evaluated in the United States for Medicare hospice care. Beyond diagnoses and residence, which information is required to establish eligibility?
o: An estimate of how much daily help his family provides
An estimate of the time elapsed since diagnosis
An estimate of prognosis if the disease follows its expected course
An estimate of the time remaining until the patient can leave hospital
explanation:
**Medicare hospice eligibility** depends on certification of terminal illness and prognosis under the disease's usual expected course. Diagnoses, family assistance, and discharge logistics do not substitute for that prognostic assessment (p. 1046). "an expected prognosis of less than 6 months “if the disease runs its usual and expected course.”" (p. 1046).

**A. An estimate of how much daily help his family provides.** Wrong, family assistance describes support needs, not the prognosis used for the certification described in the source (p. 1046).
**B. An estimate of the time elapsed since diagnosis.** Wrong, elapsed time since diagnosis does not establish the expected remaining course required for hospice certification (p. 1046).
**C. An estimate of prognosis if the disease follows its expected course.** Correct, this is the prognostic information specified for the attending physician and hospice medical director's certification (p. 1046).
**D. An estimate of the time remaining until the patient can leave hospital.** Wrong, discharge timing is not the expected prognosis of the terminal illness and does not establish the cited eligibility criterion (p. 1046).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1046.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: חולה בישראל הוגדר כחולה הנוטה למות וסובל מקוצר נשימה קשה. הוא מבקש הקלה בסבלו. איזה עיקרון תואם את סעיף 23 לחוק החולה הנוטה למות?
o: להימנע מטיפול מקל בשל הסיכון הסביר הנלווה לחיי החולה
לתת טיפול המכוון לגרימת מוות לשם הקלה על סבל החולה
לתת טיפול מקל לפי רצונו גם בסיכון סביר לחייו
להפסיק טיפול רציף אף שההפסקה עלולה להביא למות החולה
explanation:
החוק מחייב **טיפול מקל** להקלת כאב וסבל בהתאם לרצון החולה ובאמצעים ובתנאים סבירים, גם כשנלווה לכך סיכון סביר לחיים. חובה זו מובחנת מפעולה המכוונת להמית ומהפסקת טיפול רציף העלולה להביא למוות. לכן הבירור והטיפול בסבל נשארים חלק מהחובה המקצועית גם כאשר המטופל מבטא רצון להפסיק לסבול (סעיפים 19, 21, 23).
"על הרופא האחראי לגרום לכך שייעשה כל שניתן כדי להקל על כאבו וסבלו של החולה הנוטה למות, אף אם הדבר כרוך בסיכון סביר לחייו של החולה," (סעיף 23, עמ׳ PDF 12).
"אין בהוראות חוק זה כדי להתיר עשיית פעולה, אף אם היא טיפול רפואי, המכוונת להמית," (סעיף 19, עמ׳ PDF 11).

**א. להימנע מטיפול מקל בשל הסיכון הסביר הנלווה לחיי החולה.** שגויה, עצם קיומו של סיכון סביר אינו מבטל את החובה לטיפול מקל בתנאים שהחוק מפרט, סעיף 23.
**ב. לתת טיפול המכוון לגרימת מוות לשם הקלה על סבל החולה.** שגויה, החוק אוסר פעולה המכוונת להמית גם אם נעשית מתוך חמלה; היא אינה הטיפול המקל המתואר, סעיף 19.
**ג. לתת טיפול מקל לפי רצונו גם בסיכון סביר לחייו.** נכונה, זו החובה המפורשת בסעיף 23, בכפוף לרצון החולה ולתנאים ולאמצעים הסבירים.
**ד. להפסיק טיפול רציף אף שההפסקה עלולה להביא למות החולה.** שגויה, סעיף 21 אוסר הפסקת טיפול רפואי רציף העלולה להביא למוות; החובה להקל אינה מתירה פעולה זו, סעיף 21.

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, תשס״ו–2005, סעיפים 19, 21, 23; עמ׳ PDF 11–12.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: A 77-year-old man with COPD (FEV1 45%), coronary disease, and diabetes has had four admissions for COPD exacerbations in eight months. Between admissions he needs help with basic ADLs from his older wife, who is exhausted. Creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min by Cockcroft–Gault. He takes 14 medications, including warfarin requiring frequent INR testing, and says, “I am tired of the struggle.” Which referral plan explicitly integrates symptom management, discussion of care goals, and support for the family?
o: Home-health referral centered on medication administration and INR checks
Adult-day-program referral centered on activities and caregiver respite
Palliative-care review of symptoms, goals, and caregiver needs
Care-management referral centered on appointments and service coordination
explanation:
**Palliative care** addresses the patient and family’s experience of serious illness, including symptoms, stress, and care goals. Hazzard states, “Palliative care aims to improve the quality of life for both the patient with serious illness and the family” (p. 1045). Its components include symptom management, communication about goals, care coordination, and caregiver support, matching the integrated focus requested here (p. 1045).

**A. Home-health referral centered on medication administration and INR checks.** Wrong, this proposed plan addresses medication logistics but omits the explicit symptom, goals, and caregiver discussion requested (p. 1045).
**B. Adult-day-program referral centered on activities and caregiver respite.** Wrong, respite addresses one family need, but the proposed plan does not include the requested symptom and goals review (p. 1045).
**C. Palliative-care review of symptoms, goals, and caregiver needs.** Correct, this combines the source-described palliative-care domains relevant to the stated patient and caregiver burdens (p. 1045).
**D. Care-management referral centered on appointments and service coordination.** Wrong, coordination is useful but this proposed narrow focus omits the symptom and goals work included in palliative care (p. 1045).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1045.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: דיירת בית אבות בת 83 עם דמנציה מתקדמת ו-CKD שלב 3B (eGFR 35 mL/min/1.73m²) אוכלת בצורה לקויה במשך שבועות. הצוות מדווח שהיא מצניעה אוכל בפה ואיבדה 8% ממשקל גופה. פגישות משפחה מאשרות מטרות טיפול ממוקדות נוחות. בדיקות מעבדה מראות albumin 2.9 g/dL, BUN 45 mg/dL, creatinine 1.8 mg/dL. מהי ההתערבות המתאימה ביותר?
o: התחלת megestrol acetate 400 mg ביום
הנחת PEG tube לתמיכה תזונתית
יישום תוכנית האכלה ידנית מסייעת
התחלת דיאטה כלייתית עם הגבלת חלבון
explanation:
**האכלה ידנית מותאמת** היא נקודת המוצא כאשר ניתן עדיין להזין דרך הפה. המלצות משרד הבריאות מעדיפות דרך זו גם בקיהיון מתקדם, בזכות היותה דרך טבעית וההנאה מטעימת המזון, תוך התאמת הכמויות, המרקם והצרכים לכל מטופל (עמ׳ 3). כהסקה לתרחיש, ההעדפה היא לתכנית מסייעת ולהערכה תזונתית ובליעתית, ולא להנחה שכל ירידה באכילה מחייבת PEG או שכל PEG סותר טיפול נוחות (עמ׳ 3, 5–6).
"מבחינה רפואית הדרך העדיפה למתן מזון ונוזלים בכל אדם, כולל חולה עם קיהיון בשלבים מתקדמים, הוא דרך הפה." (עמ׳ 3).

**א. התחלת megestrol acetate 400 mg ביום.** שגויה, למגסטרול תועלת מועטה במשקל וסיכון לתרומבוזיס ואולי לתמותה במבוגרים; הוא אינו מחליף התאמה של ההאכלה ושל הצרכים התזונתיים (Beers 2023, עמ׳ 2062; המלצות משרד הבריאות, עמ׳ 3).
**ב. הנחת PEG tube לתמיכה תזונתית.** שגויה, לא תואר שכבר מוצתה האפשרות להזנה מספקת דרך הפה. ההמלצות דורשות בחירת דרך הזנה באופן אישי והערכה לפני מעבר להזנה מלאכותית, ולא הנחת צינור אוטומטית בגלל קיהיון (עמ׳ 3, 5–6).
**ג. יישום תוכנית האכלה ידנית מסייעת.** נכונה, ההאכלה דרך הפה היא הדרך המועדפת, עם כמויות קטנות, קצב מותאם והערכת בליעה ותזונה. היא נותנת מענה ישיר לקושי המתואר תוך שמירה על תכנית אישית (עמ׳ 3, 5).
**ד. התחלת renal diet עם הגבלת חלבון.** שגויה, הגבלת חלבון לבדה אינה מספקת עזרה באכילה ואינה מחליפה הערכת כמות והרכב המזון. יש להתאים את הצרכים באופן אישי, לרבות למחלת הכליות, ולא לבחור בהגבלה גורפת כמענה לירידה בצריכה (עמ׳ 3, 5).

מקור: המלצות מותב הוועדה הארצית לחוק החולה הנוטה למות, 11.08.2016, עמ׳ 3, 5–6; AGS Beers Criteria 2023, עמ׳ 2062.
ref: Hazzard Ch 67 — PALLIATIVE CARE AND SPECIAL MANAGEMENT ISSUES

q: אישה בת 75 עם AML שוקלת כימותרפיה. היא מבינה את המידע ויכולה לקבל החלטה, ואומרת: "אני רוצה לחיות עד סיום הלימודים של נכדתי, אבל איני רוצה לסבול." כבר נמסרה לה התועלת הצפויה. איזו שאלה תברר באופן הישיר ביותר את האיזון שהיא מבקשת בין הארכת חיים לנטל הטיפול?
o: איזה קרוב משפחה תרצי שילווה אותך ויעזור בארגון הביקורים במרפאה?
איזו דרך למתן התרופות תשתלב טוב יותר בסדר יומך?
אילו תופעות לוואי וקשיים תהיי מוכנה לשאת לשם הארכת חיים?
איזה מקום טיפול יהיה נגיש יותר מבחינת הנסיעות והלינה?
explanation:
**בחירה מדעת** מחייבת להסביר גם סיכונים, כאב, אי־נוחות וחלופות, כדי לאפשר למטופלת להחליט מרצונה. בירור מה משמעות הסבל עבורה מחבר את המידע הזה לערכים ולמטרות שלה; זו הסקה יישומית מעקרונות החוק ומעקרונות תכנון הטיפול המתוארים ב־Hazzard (סעיף 13, עמ׳ PDF 8; Hazzard עמ׳ 1052).
"הסיכונים הכרוכים בטיפול המוצע, לרבות תופעות לוואי, כאב ואי נוחות;" (עמ׳ 8).

**א. איזה קרוב משפחה תרצי שילווה אותך ויעזור בארגון הביקורים במרפאה?.** שגויה, ליווי חשוב לארגון הטיפול, אך השאלה אינה מבררת איזה נטל המטופלת מוכנה לקבל תמורת תועלת; זהו ההבדל הנדרש כאן בין סיוע מעשי לבין בירור מטרות, כהסקה מעקרונות תכנון הטיפול (עמ׳ 1052).
**ב. איזו דרך למתן התרופות תשתלב טוב יותר בסדר יומך?.** שגויה, דרך מתן תרופות היא העדפה מעשית, אך אינה מבררת את נכונותה לשאת רעילות וקשיים לשם הארכת חיים; השאלה מצמצמת את השיחה ביחס למידע על הסיכונים הנדרש בחוק (סעיף 13, עמ׳ PDF 8).
**ג. אילו תופעות לוואי וקשיים תהיי מוכנה לשאת לשם הארכת חיים?.** נכונה, השאלה מבררת ישירות מה פירוש הסבל עבורה ואיזה מחיר היא מוכנה לשלם בעד מטרתה, תוך דיון בסיכונים ובחלופות הנדרשים לבחירה מדעת (סעיף 13, עמ׳ PDF 8; Hazzard עמ׳ 1052).
**ד. איזה מקום טיפול יהיה נגיש יותר מבחינת הנסיעות והלינה?.** שגויה, נגישות המקום נוגעת לארגון הטיפול, אך אינה פותרת את המתח שהמטופלת הציגה בין התועלת לנטל; זו הסקה מעקרון התאמת הטיפול למטרותיה (עמ׳ 1052).

מקור: חוק זכויות החולה, תשנ_ו-1996.pdf 8; Hazzard 8e 1052.
ref: Hazzard 8e (marked) · p.1052

q: מה נכון לגבי הטיפול ב- Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis?
o: רוב החולים מגיבים זמנית לטיפול בסטרואידים במינון גבוה
הטיפול בשילוב של סטרואידים, azathioprine ו- N-acetylcysteine הוכח כמפחית אשפוזים אך לא כמאריך תוחלת חיים
הטיפול ב- pirfenidone משפר איכות חיים אך ללא השפעה משמעותית על מהלך המחלה
יש לשלב טיפול פליאטיבי משלב מוקדם של המחלה
explanation:
**Palliative care accompanies disease-directed treatment** according to symptoms and needs; it is not restricted to the final days of life. Symptoms and psychological burden in IPF can persist during antifibrotic treatment, supporting early integrated care (Mackintosh 2024; read from the paper) (Symptom management and palliative care). **Antifibrotics** slow lung-function decline but do not reverse established scarring (Hazzard 8e, p. 1231).
"In IPF and PPF, symptomatic care should be initiated early and can aid in the delivery of bad news." (Mackintosh 2024; read from the paper) (Symptom management and palliative care)
"The antifibrotic medications slow the progression of restriction in lung function studies, but do not reverse any scarring that has already occurred." (Hazzard 8e, p. 1231)

**A. Most patients temporarily respond to high-dose steroids.** Wrong, Hazzard describes a primarily fibrotic disease whose treatment centers on antifibrotics rather than chronic steroids; it does not support the claim that most patients respond to high-dose steroids (p. 1231).
**B. Steroids, azathioprine, and N-acetylcysteine reduce hospitalizations without prolonging survival.** Wrong, PANTHER-IPF found increased death and hospitalization with this combination compared with placebo, contradicting the claim of fewer hospitalizations: "Increased risks of death and hospitalization were observed in patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis" (Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis Clinical Research Network 2012; read from the paper) (Abstract, Conclusions; Results).
**C. Pirfenidone improves quality of life without significantly altering disease course.** Wrong, pirfenidone slows deterioration of lung function, although symptoms and quality of life may not improve immediately. Inference: the proposed statement confuses modification of disease course with immediate symptomatic relief (Hazzard 8e, p. 1231).
**D. Integrate palliative care early in the disease.** Correct, early symptom-directed and supportive care addresses disease burden alongside disease-directed treatment. Inference: specialist palliative involvement should be guided by unmet needs rather than abandonment of disease treatment (Mackintosh 2024; read from the paper) (Symptom management and palliative care).

The book describes IPF as steadily progressive, with high morbidity and mortality and median survival of only a few years after diagnosis, even with treatment (Hazzard 8e, p. 1231). The principle of early palliative care concurrent with disease-focused treatment is described on p. 1047 in advanced lung cancer; that passage is not IPF-specific.

q: מה נכון לגבי טיפול לא תרופתי בקוצר נשימה בסוף החיים ?
o: במחקר שהשווה מתן אויר לעומת חמצן דרך משקפים ( nasal cannula) לחולים עם סטורציה תקינה, נמצא יתרון משמעותי למתן חמצן
טיפול בהנשמה לא פולשנית מסוג BiPAP אינו מומלץ לחולי COPD בדרגה מתקדמת
טיפול בחמצן לחולי COPD עם ירידה בריווי חמצן משפר איכות חיים ומאריך חיים
בחולים אונקולוגים לא נמצא יתרון בשיפור איכות חיים בטיפול בהנשמה לא פולשנית
explanation:
In COPD with **hypoxia**, long-term oxygen improves quality of life and survival. This does not imply that oxygen is superior to air when hypoxia is absent (p. 1074).

**A. Oxygen through a nasal cannula was significantly better than air in patients with normal saturation.** Wrong, in nonhypoxic patients there was no difference in dyspnea relief between nasal-cannula oxygen and air (p. 1074).
**B. Noninvasive BiPAP is not recommended in advanced COPD.** Wrong, the book describes a COPD subgroup in which noninvasive ventilation improves quality of life and survival; a general rejection is inappropriate (p. 1074).
**C. Oxygen improves quality of life and prolongs life in hypoxic COPD.** Correct, this ties treatment to hypoxia, the population in which the source describes these benefits (p. 1074).
**D. Noninvasive ventilation has shown no quality-of-life benefit in cancer patients.** Wrong, in advanced cancer the source reports less dyspnea and lower morphine requirements, alongside mask-tolerance problems. This does not support a blanket denial of benefit (p. 1074).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1074.

q: בן 82, עם קרצינומה גרורתית של הערמונית, מוגדר כנוטה למות במצב סופי, עם פצע לחץ דרגה 4 בעכוז, בגודל של 12X11 ס"מ, עומק של 2 ס"מ, עם קטעים נקרוטיים והפרשה מזוהמת בכמות רבה עם ריח אופנסיבי. המשפחה והשכן לחדר מתלוננים על. הריח י מה הגישה המומלצת במקרה זה להפחתת הריחות?
o: החלפת חבישות פולידין פעמיים ביום
שימוש טופיקלי בתכשיר Metronidazole
ביצוע הטריה כירורגית של הפצע
החלפת חבישה בתדירות גבוהה מהרגיל
explanation:
**Topical metronidazole** is explicitly recommended for malodorous drainage in palliative pressure-injury care. The goals are comfort and reducing wound burden, using absorptive dressings to reduce dressing changes and prioritizing pain relief (p. 698).

**A. Change povidone-iodine dressings twice daily.** Wrong, the odor-specific recommendation is metronidazole, with absorptive dressings to reduce changes; this povidone-iodine schedule is not the recommended odor treatment (p. 698).
**B. Apply topical metronidazole.** Correct, metronidazole placed in the wound is explicitly recommended for odorous drainage as part of comfort-focused care (p. 698).
**C. Surgical wound debridement.** Wrong, debridement of necrotic tissue may be part of palliative care, but the specific odor treatment is local metronidazole; the source does not require a surgical procedure for this purpose (p. 698).
**D. Change dressings more frequently than usual.** Wrong, highly absorptive dressings are preferred to reduce the frequency and burden of changes. More frequent changes do not provide the targeted odor treatment (p. 698).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 698.

q: מה נכון לגבי קוצר נשימה DYSPNEA בסוף החיים?
o: חומרת קוצר הנשימה נמצאת בקשר ישיר לרמת ירידת הסטורציה בדם
בחולים ללא היפוקסיה מזרם אויר יעיל להקלה כמו זרם חמצן
מחלות נוירולוגיות גורמות לקוצר נשימה במנגנון של VENTILATION/PERFUSION MISMATCH
שכיח בחולי אי ספיקת לב ו- COPD אך נדיר בחולי דמנציה
explanation:
Official answer: ב

**Dyspnea is subjective** and is not always correlated with hypoxia, hypercarbia or tachypnea (p. 1073). In the cited study of nonhypoxic patients, air and oxygen were both delivered by nasal cannula and gave no different relief. A fan is mentioned separately as a nonpharmacologic measure; this study must not be described as comparing oxygen with a fan or an open window (p. 1074).

**A. Dyspnea severity directly correlates with the fall in oxygen saturation.** Wrong, oxygen saturation alone does not grade the subjective distress; dyspnea need not track hypoxia, hypercarbia or tachypnea (p. 1073).
**B. In nonhypoxic patients, airflow relieves dyspnea as effectively as oxygen.** Correct, the cited study found no difference between nasal-cannula air and nasal-cannula oxygen in patients without hypoxia; this is the comparison supporting the option (p. 1074).
**C. Neurologic diseases cause dyspnea through ventilation/perfusion mismatch.** Wrong, multiple sclerosis and motor neuron disease are examples of respiratory-system weakness in the source, not of ventilation/perfusion mismatch (p. 1073).
**D. Common in heart failure and COPD but rare in dementia.** Wrong, the source also describes bothersome dyspnea in older adults with dementia, so restricting the problem to heart failure or COPD and calling it rare in dementia is unsupported (p. 1082).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1073, 1074, 1082.

q: במטופל עם מחלה מסכנת חיים, מהי אינדיקציה להזמנת יעוץ פליאטיבי לחולה ביום הראשון לאשפוזו?
o: גיל מעל 90
כאב המצריך טיפול באופיואידים
דליריום
אשפוז עקב אותה הבעיה לפני חודש
explanation:
**Official answer:** Pain requiring opioids; delirium; admission for the same problem one month earlier (IMA final answer key, May 2024, question 84).
The day-one consultation flowchart includes **repeated admission for the same reason** in recent months. The current admission plus another for the same problem one month earlier meets this criterion. For pain and psychological symptoms, the flowchart adds difficulty controlling symptoms, which is not established by every opioid requirement or every delirium episode in the question (p. 1082, Figure 70-3). Delirium was added to the post-appeal key (IMA, May 2024, question 84).

**A. Age over 90.** Wrong, age alone is not an admission-day criterion; the flowchart focuses on needs, symptoms and the pattern of admissions (p. 1082).
**B. Pain requiring opioids.** Correct, for official scoring. The source conditions symptom-related referral on difficulty controlling symptoms; an opioid requirement alone does not establish that condition, as explained above (p. 1082).
**C. Delirium.** Correct, for official scoring. Delirium can create symptom-management needs, but the flowchart requires difficulty controlling symptoms, not the diagnosis alone; this qualification remains (p. 1082).
**D. Admission for the same problem one month earlier.** Correct, the previous and current admissions for the same problem fit the recent repeated-admission criterion (p. 1082).

q: כל הטיפולים הבאים פרט לאחד אפשריים לטיפול תומך בקוצר נשימה, בחולה שקוע הכרתית עם COPD מתקדם, במסגרת טיפול סוף חיים. איזה טיפול לא מתאים?
o: אופיואידים
מאוורר
CPAP
סטרואידים
explanation:
**CPAP** is the officially accepted exception. The source discusses benefit from noninvasive support in some patients alongside mask intolerance and anxiety; it does not establish a universal prohibition (p. 1074).

**A. Opioids.** Wrong, this is not the exception: opioids may relieve refractory dyspnea despite optimal underlying-disease treatment, with benefit weighed against adverse effects (p. 1074).
**B. A fan.** Wrong, this is not the exception: a fan is among the nonpharmacologic measures that may relieve breathlessness (p. 1074).
**C. CPAP.** Correct, officially accepted as the unsuitable treatment. The source describes discontinuation of noninvasive support because of anxiety and mask intolerance; that does not prove a blanket prohibition in every patient (p. 1074).
**D. Corticosteroids.** Wrong, this is not the exception: inhaled corticosteroids are included in the advanced-COPD dyspnea table, but this does not mean that every corticosteroid suits every cause of dyspnea (p. 1263).

Suitability of noninvasive support depends on goals and tolerance; the source describes benefit for some patients alongside mask intolerance and anxiety (p. 1074).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1074, 1263.
